title: CloudTrail & Audit Logging
summary: Record every API call, prove logs weren't tampered with, and centralize logs across accounts.
tldr: **CloudTrail** records *who did what, when and from where* for AWS API calls. Management events are on by default; **data events** (S3 object reads, Lambda invokes) must be added to a trail.
For many accounts, create one **organization trail** delivering to an S3 bucket in a separate **log archive account**. Member-account admins can't stop or delete it.
Turn on **log file integrity validation** to prove log files weren't changed or deleted after delivery.

keyFacts.text: **Event history** keeps the last 90 days of management events per Region for free, with no trail. Longer retention needs a trail to S3 or CloudTrail Lake.
Integrity validation writes hourly **digest files** signed with SHA-256 hashes, so you can detect any modified, deleted or missing log file.
High-volume operations such as S3 `GetObject` or Lambda `Invoke` are **not logged by default**. Add them with advanced event selectors, scoped to specific ARNs.
**CloudTrail Insights** learns the normal rate of write API calls (or error rate) and raises an event when activity deviates, with no thresholds to set.
CloudTrail logs API calls, not packets. Accepted or rejected connections between IPs come from **VPC Flow Logs**.

keywords.cue: record API activity from all current and future accounts
prove log files were not modified or deleted
workload admins must not be able to stop logging
keywords.answer: Organization trail in a separate log archive account (plus SCP)

keywords.cue: which principals downloaded objects from a bucket
record every invocation of specific Lambda functions
keywords.answer: CloudTrail Lambda data events via advanced event selectors

keywords.cue: alert when API call volume deviates from baseline
least-privilege policy from what the role actually used
keywords.answer: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail

keywords.cue: show which tenant each KMS Decrypt call was for
separation of duties for a KMS key
keywords.answer: Key policy splitting admin actions from cryptographic actions

traps: S3 Versioning on per-account buckets doesn't stop a local admin from deleting the trail itself.
Exporting event history with a scheduled Lambda is more work and misses events older than 90 days.
An AWS Config aggregator collects configuration items, not API activity. It is not a substitute for CloudTrail.
GuardDuty and AWS Config don't record each Lambda invocation. Use CloudTrail data events.
Allowing `kms:*` to everyone and alerting afterwards is detection, not separation of duties.
